To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nodular amyloidoma (NA) of lung is a non-neoplastic reactive lymphoplasmacellular lesion with eosinophilic amayloid deposits and a B-cell CLL/SLL-like infiltrate, while primary malignant lymphomas of the lung with amyloid production (MLA) are low-grade B-cell NHL with secondary amayloid production.
nodular amyloidomas of the lung can be separated from primary pulmonary lymphomas with amyloid production using a combination of histologic and immunophistochemical features.

nodular amyloidomas of the lung can be separated from primary low-grade malignant lung lymphomas with secondary amyloid production utilizing histologic features including lymphatic tracking, pleural involvement, sheet-like masses of reactive plasma cells and reactive follicles, and immunophenotype including a dominant T-cell population, absence of light chain restriction, and lack of aberrant antigen expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential diagnosis of NA and ML.
a differential diagnostic problem between nodular amyloidoma and malignant lymphoma of the lung.
the differential diagnosis of nodular amyloidosis and low grade malignant lymphoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a lymphoproliferation with amyloid production should be considered as a lymphoma if the following histologic features are present: (1) a lymphoplasmatic cell population with a B-cell immunophenotype; (2) a lymphoplasicytic infiltrate with a CD20+, CD43+ phenotype; (3) a light chain-restricted population; (4) a lymphoplascytic infiltrate with follicular growth pattern; (5) a pleural infiltrate;
NA and ML are not the same entity, but that they are closely associated with each other.
the presence of a lymphoid infiltrate with a B-cell immunophenotype and light chain restriction in an amyloidoma should raise the possibility of a low-grade lymphoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of a lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate with a reactive pattern, a non-neoplastic lymphatic distribution and a lack of CD20 expression should raise suspicion for a diagnosis of nodular amyloidoma.

a reactive lymphoplaseracytic infiltrate with amyloid deposits is not a neoplastic process, and that the presence of an underlying neoplastic lymphoid process should be considered in any case of amyloidoma.

the presence of lymphatic tracking, pleural infiltration, a sheet-like mass of plasma cells and reactive follicles in a lesion composed predominantly of CD20+, CD45+, CD79a+, CD20+/- CD43+/- B cells is highly suggestive of a primary low-grade malignant B-cell lymphoma with secondary amyloid production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of amyloid in a pulmonary mass does not necessarily imply a nonneoplastic etiology.
the differential diagnosis between NA and ML can be made on the basis of the histopathologic and immunochemical features of the cellular component.
the presence of a lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in a pulmonary mass with amyloid deposition should raise the suspicion of a low-grade malignant lymphoma.
